title: Intersection Observer
definition: A browser API that provides a way to asynchronously observe changes in the intersection of a target element with an ancestor element or with a top-level document's viewport.
simpleExplanation: Instead of using a scroll listener that fires 1000 times a second to do complex math to ask 'Is this image on the screen yet?', you hire a security guard (Intersection Observer). You tell the guard, 'Tap me on the shoulder the exact second this image enters the screen.'
realWorldExample: Infinite Scrolling. You place an invisible `<div>` at the bottom of your list. When the Intersection Observer sees that `<div>` enter the screen, it fetches the next page of API results.

basic: Why is Intersection Observer better than a `scroll` event listener?
advanced: How do you stop observing an element once it has loaded?

answers.question: Why is it better than a scroll listener?
answers.answer: Scroll listeners run synchronously on the main thread, causing severe performance jank. Intersection Observer runs asynchronously off the main thread, vastly improving performance.

answers.question: What is the threshold?
answers.answer: It is a number between 0 and 1 indicating how much of the element must be visible before the callback fires. `0` means '1 pixel has entered'. `1.0` means 'The entire element is 100% visible on screen'.
